newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies saw 1.5 to 12 inches snow, cold.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies saw 1.5 to 12 inches snow, cold.

text.p: Canada's Prairies Wednesday saw overnight lows as cold as -13 Celsius (8.6 F) in Saskatchewan where 53 percent of harvest was complete and 4 cm (1.6 inches) to 30 cm (11.8 inches) of snow, Environment Canada said.
"We're not going to see anywhere near as much precipitation on the Prairies today, that system is well into Ontario now," meteorologist Steve Smith said.
The entire Prairie grainbelt saw a killing frost overnight and snowfall, Smith said.
Harvest was stalled for one to three weeks on wet weather.
Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete, Saskatchewan combined 53 percent of crops and Manitoba had 75 percent of crops in the bin by Sept 30, according to provincial agriculture reports.
Alberta was forecast to see warmer temperatures with cloudy skies and highs of seven to 10 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see clearing skies with some snow flurries and highs of 0 to six Celsius.
Manitoba was forecast to see some snow flurries with highs of 0 to six Celsius.
